title: Footnotes Gone Feral
blurb: The parts of history your textbook skipped because nobody would believe them.

cards.say: [Ice hockey made its Olympic debut at the 1920 Summer Games], [a Japanese marathoner who quit at the 1912 Olympics finished the race in 1967], [a runner in the 1904 Olympic marathon rode part of the way in a car], and [the five-ring Olympic flag first flew at the 1896 Athens Games].
cards.real: Pierre de Coubertin designed the five-ring flag in 1913, and it first flew at an Olympic Games in Antwerp in 1920.

cards.say: [Herbert Hoover and his wife spoke Chinese in the White House for privacy], [Thomas Jefferson was the first president to live in the White House], [Calvin Coolidge adopted a raccoon that was sent to be his Thanksgiving dinner], and [Chester Arthur sent 24 wagonloads of White House furniture to auction].
cards.real: John Adams moved into the White House in November 1800, a few months before Jefferson took office.

cards.say: [The Pony Express carried mail across the West for twelve years], [in 1914 a little girl in Idaho was mailed to her grandparents], [the US Navy and Post Office once delivered mail by cruise missile], and [the Hope Diamond was mailed to the Smithsonian wrapped in brown paper].
cards.real: The Pony Express ran for only about 19 months, from April 1860 to November 1861. The telegraph put it out of business.

cards.say: [Julius Caesar was kidnapped by pirates, then came back and captured them], [the Roman emperor Claudius added three new letters to the alphabet], [Alexander the Great was personally tutored as a teenager by Plato], and [a San Francisco man proclaimed himself Emperor of the United States in 1859].
cards.real: Alexander's teenage tutor was Aristotle, a former student of Plato. Plato had died years earlier, when Alexander was a young boy.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Aristotle tutored Alexander from 343 BC; Plato died about 347 BC) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great
NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Joshua Norton proclaimed himself Emperor of the United States on September 17, 1859) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_Norton

cards.say: [The first tomato ketchup recipe was invented by Henry Heinz], [the oldest known potato chip recipe is from an 1817 English cookbook], [nachos are named after the man who first served them in 1943], and [early English ketchups were made from mushrooms or walnuts].
cards.real: The first published tomato ketchup recipe came from Philadelphia scientist James Mease in 1812. Heinz didn't start selling ketchup until 1876.

cards.say: [Julia Child worked for a US spy agency before she became a chef], [J.R.R. Tolkien once worked on the Oxford English Dictionary], [Florence Nightingale was the first person ever to draw a pie chart], and [Marie Curie's notebooks are still radioactive and kept in lead-lined boxes].
cards.real: William Playfair drew the first known pie chart in 1801, almost 20 years before Nightingale was born. Her famous chart was the rose diagram.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Child worked for the OSS in World War II) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child

cards.say: [Stonehenge was sold at a public auction in 1915 for 6,600 pounds], [the first stone of Notre-Dame in Paris was laid by a pope], [the Empire State Building's spire was built as a dock for airships], and [the Washington Monument was finished in time for the US centennial in 1876].
cards.real: Work stopped in 1854 when donations ran out and only restarted in 1877, so the stone tower wasn't finished until 1884.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: the spire was designed as a mooring mast for dirigibles) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_State_Building

cards.say: [When the Mona Lisa was stolen in 1911, police questioned Pablo Picasso], [Mozart wrote the tune of Twinkle Twinkle Little Star at age five], [Napoleon wrote a romantic novella years before he became emperor], and [the first Academy Awards ceremony lasted just 15 minutes].
cards.real: The melody is an old French folk song. Mozart wrote a set of variations on it in his twenties, which is why it gets credited to him.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: the tune is the French song Ah! vous dirai-je, maman; Mozart's variations date from his twenties) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twinkle,_Twinkle,_Little_Star

cards.say: [The world's first parking meter was installed in Oklahoma City in 1935], [the world's first traffic light exploded less than a month after it went up], [London's first underground railway opened after the US Civil War ended], and [the first cat to reach space was launched by France in 1963].
cards.real: London's Metropolitan Railway, the world's first underground railway, opened in January 1863, more than two years before the US Civil War ended.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: the first parking meter went in on July 16, 1935, in Oklahoma City) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parking_meter

cards.say: [Three of the first five US presidents died on the Fourth of July], [the Continental Congress voted for independence on July 2, 1776], [the White House didn't get its official name until 1901], and [the Liberty Bell got its famous name during the American Revolution].
cards.real: It was just the State House bell until abolitionists started calling it the Liberty Bell in the 1830s, as a symbol of the fight to end slavery.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Congress approved the Lee Resolution for independence on July 2, 1776) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Resolution

cards.say: [Albert Einstein won his Nobel Prize for the theory of relativity], [Liquid Paper was invented by the mother of one of the Monkees], [Kleenex was first sold in 1924 as a way to remove cold cream], and [a British man who never visited the US paid to found the Smithsonian].
cards.real: Einstein's 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for his explanation of the photoelectric effect, not for relativity.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: James Smithson never set foot in the US) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Smithson

cards.say: [The only casualty of the 1859 Pig War between the US and Britain was a pig], [the Pilgrims wore shiny buckles on the front of their hats], [Monopoly sets smuggled escape maps to prisoners of war in World War II], and [the US bought Alaska from Russia for about two cents an acre].
cards.real: Pilgrim hats never had buckles. The buckled Pilgrim hat was invented by artists in the 1800s.
